newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany still has time to meet EMU goals - banker.
newsitem.headline: Germany still has time to meet EMU goals - banker.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Ulrich Cartellieri said on Wednesday that there were grounds for fearing Germany might not qualify for Europe's planned monetary union but there was still time to meet the criteria.
"Germany can still reach the three percent deficit criterion without ifs and buts," Cartellieri told the bank's annual news conference.
Swift action was need to close a 10 billion-mark budget gap and to end political wrangling over tax and pension reforms which was blocking domestic investment, Cartellieri said.

Doubts are growing about Germany's ability to reduce its budget deficit below the limit of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) during 1997, the crucial year for deciding who qualifies to launch the planned single currency on January 1, 1999. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
